 J U D G M E N T

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 30.05.2024 at about 12.10 p.m., she was walking along with her father on the road side at HBR Layout, BDA Complex and when they reached near Meenakshi Hotel, Bengaluru, a Royal Enfield Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KC-3885, ridden by its rider, at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the petitioner.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, she was shifted to B.R.Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .2,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant, conveyance and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was a student.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, both the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondents have denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondents have also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondents have contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further respondent No.1 contended that they have issued two wheeler bundled Policy bearing No.3410/0043546/000/00 in favour of second respondent in respect of vehicle bearing Engine No.U3ssf1LH357262 and Chassis No.ME3U3S5F1LH129965 valid from 17.09.2020 to 16.09.2021 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.

Further contended that the owner of two wheeler/insured had been willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license, fitness certificate, to drive the same as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2, in the written statement, has contended that the petitioner was crossing the road without observing the movement of vehicles on said road and there was no zebra crossing lines or traffic signals on the said road.

The 2nd respondent was moving slowly and cautiously at a normal speed and at that time, the petitioner without noticing the vehicle of this respondent, tried to cross the road and came against the vehicle of respondent No.2 and sustained injuries.
Further petitioner alone responsible for the said alleged accident.

Further contended that after the accident,
immediately the 2nd respondent came to the rescue of petitioner on humanitarian grounds and also having courtesy over the said petitioner, the 2nd respondent took her to Dr.B.R.Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital and he admitted her as inpatient.

Immediately, after her admission as inpatient, the respondent No.2 spoke to concerned doctors and requested them to provide necessary treatment to the petitioner and thereby he paid .27,000/- on the same day towards medical bills.

Further, respondent No.2 made other arrangements for stay of petitioner at the said hospital and thereafter, periodically visited the hospital and paid the subsequent bills to the said hospital over a sum of .1,40,000/-.

Further the payment of medical expenses for a period of 35 days, this 2nd respondent has paid .1,000/- per day to the petitioner's father and totally he has paid .35,000/-
to the petitioner's father and mother till she got discharged from the said hospital.
The other amount of .1,000/- was paid at the hand of her father Sri.Lachamappa and mother Smt.Shantamma.
Therefore, the 2nd respondent has borne the entire medical expenses of the petitioner.
Accordingly, the petitioner's parents have not spent any amount towards her treatment.

Further contended that the petitioner is not entitled to get compensation of a sum of .10,00,000/-
at the hands of respondent.
In addition to that the vehicle of 2nd respondent is insured with the 1st respondent insurance company.
Further as on the date of accident, the vehicle was insured and the policy was in force from the period from 17.09.2020 to 16.09.2025.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 30.05.2024 at about 12.10 p.m., when petitioner was going along with her father as a pedestrian, Opp Meenakshi Hotel, Near BDA Complex, HBR Layout,
Bengaluru City, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of Royal Enfield Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KC-3885 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

7. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the Natural Guardian/father of minor petitioner examined as PW.1 and Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center got examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to 12 and closed their side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

sentences.text: 8. Heard the argument of both side and perused the materials available on record.

The petitioner has contended that on 30.05.2024 at about 12.10 p.m., accident occurred when she was walking along with her father, Opp Meenakshi Hotel, Near BDA Complex,
HBR Layout, Bengaluru City, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of Royal Enfield Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KC-3885 by its rider in which she sustained grievous injuries.
11. In order to prove rash and negligent riding of Royal Enfield Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04- KC-3885 by its rider, the father of petitioner got examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.
12. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.2, first information statement.
On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, the mother of petitioner by name Smt.Shanthamma W/o Lakshmana has lodged complaint with police on 30.05.2024.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of offending vehicle by its rider.
The FIR is registered against the rider of offending vehicle which does not appear to have been challenged or questioned in any manner.
The petitioner also furnished spot Mahazar & sketch, which are marked as Ex.P.3 & 4.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the facts, as described in the mahazar and sketch, are contrary to the actual facts at the place of accident.
Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to vehicle are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of damages being caused to the offending vehicle.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicle.
The said document indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence Pooja vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22841426/
4 punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC marked at Ex.P.8.

sentences.text: In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The rider or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The rider or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
The respondents contended that the petitioner was also negligent and she also contributed negligence in the cause of accident.
The materials on record are not sufficient and satisfactory in order to consider the aspect of negligence on the part of petitioner in the cause of accident.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to prove the aspect of negligence on the part of petitioner in the cause of accident.
The contention of respondents is not duly substantiated by cogent and corroborative materials.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.8,
this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Royal Enfield Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KC-3885 by its rider and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:

As discussed above, the petitioner succeeded in establishing her contention that the accident took place due to negligence on the part of riding of Royal Enfield Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KC-3885 by its rider.
As the petitioner succeeded in establishing that the accident took place due to negligence of rider of motor cycle, the petitioner is entitled for compensation for the said accident.

In order to assess the compensation, several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during the treatment,
disability, loss of amenities etc., have to be taken into consideration.
15. The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained injuries and said injuries are grievous in nature.
In order to prove the injuries sustained by her, the guardian of petitioner produced wound certificate and discharge summary, which are marked at Ex.P.6 and 7.

As per discharge summary, petitioner sustained closed displaced fracture of midshaft of right femur and underwent closed reduction and internal fixation with titanium elastic nailing under short general anesthesia done on 31.05.2024 and later discharged and she took treatment as an inpatient from 30.05.2024 to 22.06.2024 i.e., for a period of 24 days.
The respondent does not appear to have disputed the nature of injuries caused to the petitioner.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to disprove or disbelieve the documents furnished by the petitioner related to the injuries sustained by her.
16. PW.2/Doctor deposed in his evidence that, petitioner has sustained closed displaced fracture of the right femur and underwent closed reduction and ten and later discharged.
Further PW.2 deposed that petitioner come up with complains of unable to walk fast, sit down, squat and sit cross leg.
17. PW.2 examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
The doctor has assessed the disability for right lower limb at 40% and to the whole body at 13%.
PW.2 stated in the cross examination that the fracture is united.
18. In the petition the age of the petitioner by name Kum.Pooja is shown as 10 years.
In order to prove the age of the petitioner, notarized copy of Aadhaar Card is furnished which is marked as Ex.P.10, wherein date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 19.09.2014.
As per the materials on record, the accident occurred on 30.05.2024 and the age of petitioner is 10 years as on the date of accident.
No contrary materials are being placed before the court in order to doubt or dispute the age of petitioner.
On consideration of materials placed before the court, the age of the petitioner is considered to be 10 years as on the date of accident.
19. In the Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Ltd and another, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the disability is upto 10% to the whole body .1 lakh, above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, .3 lakhs, upto 60%, .4 lakhs, Upto 90% .5 lakhs and above 90% it should be .6 lakhs.
For all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc.
20. Case on hand the doctor gave disability 13% to the whole body.
As per Master Mallikarjun case from 10 to 30% - .3 lakhs.

Accordingly the petitioner is entitled for .3,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock,
hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.

21. Towards Medical Expenses:

sentences.text: The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.

The petitioner contended that she has spent more than .1,50,000/- towards her medical,
conveyance and transportation charges.
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.9 for .14,413/-.
The medical bills have not been controverted or rebutted by respondents in any manner.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for .14,413/- under the head medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization.

22. Towards loss of income for parents during treatment:
The petitioner has contended that her daughter was student and she has hospitalized due to injuries sustained by her in the Road Traffic Accident.
So, when the father/mother of the petitioner was in the hospital along with petitioner, she has no income for her livelihood during that period.

As such the petitioner is entitled for lump sum of .30,000/-
under the head Discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization.

sentences.text: Regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and is in force as on the date of accident.

Therefore,
the first respondent, being the insurer and the second respondent, being the R.C owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
However, the Respondent No.1, being the insurer, is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount with interest from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:

In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to pass the following final order:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of MV Act is allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of .3,44,413/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Forty Four Thousand Four Hundred and Thirteen only) with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Entire compensation amount shall be kept in FD in the name of minor petitioner in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till she attain the age of majority whichever is later.
The guardian of petitioner is entitled to receive interest that accrues on FD periodically.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
Advocates' fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
